about.title: Lemoore Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath in Lemoore often stretches out for weeks or months as injured people deal with medical appointments and missed work. Whether the hazard was a wet floor near N Lemoore Avenue businesses, uneven pavement outside a Hanford Armona Road shopping center, or a poorly lit stairwell, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have reasonably known, about the danger and fail to fix or warn about it? That's called notice, and it's often the deciding factor in whether a claim moves forward. Because evidence like surveillance footage, incident reports, and even the condition of the flooring can change or disappear quickly, documenting what happened matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we connect injured Lemoore residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the notice issue and help gather the proof needed before it's gone.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Your Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on showing the property owner had actual or constructive notice of the hazard. An attorney can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or inspection records that speak to this.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage Before It's Erased
items.desc: Many Lemoore businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced by your percentage of responsibility but isn't automatically barred. An attorney can help address any argument that you contributed to the fall.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Lemoore?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a public building or park in Kings County, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Talking with an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical window.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover even if you share some responsibility, though your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall at a Lemoore store or apartment complex?
items.answer: If possible, take photos of the hazard, get contact information for any witnesses, and ask that any incident report be documented in writing. Reporting the fall to the property manager or business creates a record, which can support a claim later.
